editorialDecl.p: Complete English translation; spelling and names follow readable English conventions. Your Worships renders the variable civic honorifics approximately; mayors renders Stetmeister without implying identity with a modern mayoralty. Predictive Astronomia/Astronomei is generally translated astrology, with the historical overlap of astronomy and astrology acknowledged. Historical assertions and attributed authorities are translated as presented, without endorsing or authenticating them.

Editorial English paragraph divisions and punctuation do not reproduce printed lineation. Each translationSegment div has @corresp linking the first and last German xml:id in an inclusive source-line range; a single link denotes one line. The ranges cover all transcribed lines exactly once. Brackets mark explanatory supplies or tentative readings; the end notes discuss uncertainties. Source images and their provenance remain linked in the German TEI. No missing preface is reconstructed.

div.head: Anton Brelochs: English translation of the dedicatory preface for 1532

div.p: To the honorable, prudent, respected, and wise mayors and council of the city of Schwäbisch Hall, my gracious and dear lords.

Honorable, prudent, respected, and wise lords: I first offer Your Worships my most willing and diligent service. Gracious and dear lords, I have once again undertaken, so far as my limited understanding permits, to disclose what the course of the heavens signifies for us in the year 1532, and have condensed it as briefly as possible into a small prognostication. I know no one to whom I could more fittingly dedicate this judgment than Your Worships. I therefore ask that you graciously accept from me these future events, thus briefly assembled, and interpret them with your customary kindness. May you also continue to regard me as commended to your care as your humble and willing servant. Dated on the Sunday after St. Bartholomew’s Day, the twenty-seventh of August, in the year 1531.
Your Worships’ obedient servant, Dr. Antonius Brelochs.

div.head: Translation notes
div.note: Judicium means an astrological judgment or forecast here.
The weekday, feast reference, and date are retained as printed; no calendar conversion is imposed.
